item.title: CALYPR
item.description:
CALYPR is a genomics data science platform built for hybrid cloud and on-premises infrastructure. Based on the Gen3 Data Commons architecture, it combines open standards with tools for managing data, running workflows, and supporting biological discovery.

Its open-source tools include GRIP for graph-based data integration, Funnel for distributed task execution, Syfon for data registration and transfer, and Git-DRS for versioned data workflows. Learn more at calypr.org or browse the CALYPR GitHub organization.

item.title: AnVIL
item.description:
The NHGRI Genomic Data Science Analysis, Visualization, and Informatics Lab-Space (AnVIL) provides a shared environment for working with genomic data in the cloud. By bringing data and scalable computing together, AnVIL supports collaborative analysis without requiring researchers to move large datasets between institutions.

AnVIL is a collaboration among Oregon Health & Science University, the University of California, Santa Cruz, the University of Chicago, the Broad Institute, Washington University in St. Louis, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, Johns Hopkins University, and Pennsylvania State University. See the AnVIL project site for current tools and data resources.

item.title: GRIP
item.description:
GRaph Integration Platform (GRIP) provides a graph interface over several database technologies, including PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Badger, and LevelDB. Vertices and edges can carry properties and represent different kinds of relationships.

GRIP includes an API for traversing, analyzing, and updating graphs, with a query syntax inspired by Apache TinkerPop. The GRIP project on GitHub contains the code and documentation.

item.title: BMEG
item.description:
The BioMedical Evidence Graph (BMEG) was designed to bring heterogeneous biomedical data into a unified graph for discovery and machine-learning analyses. Its model connects projects, donors, samples, molecular measurements, and treatment evidence, making relationships across data sources queryable together.

The project focused on cancer genomics data, including resources such as the National Cancer Institute’s Genomic Data Commons, with the goal of supporting analyses of clinically relevant outcomes. Its distributed graph database was designed to store and query large graphs across multiple machines.

item.title: Funnel
item.description:
Funnel is a toolkit for distributed task execution with a simple API. A task records its metadata, state, input and output files, resource requests, commands, and logs. Funnel queues tasks, schedules them to workers, and tracks their progress.

A worker downloads task inputs, runs the requested containerized commands, uploads outputs, and emits events and logs. Funnel supports a range of storage and scheduling back ends, including cloud services and HPC schedulers such as HTCondor and Slurm. Read the Funnel documentation for details.
